key_insight: BrainVLM is a multimodal vision-language model that classifies all 12 WHO 2021 brain tumor types from preoperative MRI data while also quantifying uncertainty and generating radiology-style explanations.
clinical_relevance: The model is designed to support more consistent presurgical brain tumor diagnosis and could assist clinicians by improving interpretability and confidence in complex cases.
method: Trained on MRI scans, demographics, and radiology reports from 40,043 individuals.
Validated on 5,211 pathologically confirmed patients across one primary hospital hold-out set and 11 independent hospitals.
Tested in both a blinded multi-reader study with 12 neuroradiologists and a prospective real-world cohort of 1,009 patients; also assessed for molecular subgroup prediction in gliomas.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports large-scale external validation and real-world evaluation, including 5,211 confirmed cases and prospective comparison with radiologists.
watch_item: Performance may depend on local imaging protocols, workflow integration, and careful monitoring of uncertainty outputs before clinical deployment.
paper_title: A Vision-Language Foundation Model for Precise and Comprehensive Brain Tumor Diagnosis from Preoperative Multimodal Data
